items.title: Multiplying a Fraction by a Whole Number
items.explanation: To multiply a fraction by a whole number, first find the distance covered in one unit of time (e.g., 1 hour) by dividing the total distance by the denominator. Then, multiply this result by the numerator of the multiplier to get the final answer. For example, if Aaron walks 3 km in 1 hour, his speed is 3/1 km/hour. To find the distance in 2/5 hours, first divide 3 km into 5 parts to get 3/5 km per hour, then multiply by 2 to get 6/5 km.

items.title: Multiplying Two Fractions
items.explanation: When multiplying two fractions, represent the fraction as a region on a unit square. Divide the numerator of the first fraction into the denominator of the second fraction to find the shaded area. For instance, if the tortoise walks 1/4 km in 1 hour and you want to know how far it walks in 1/2 hour, divide the 1/4 region into 2 parts to get 1/8 km. The general rule is (a/b) × (c/d) = (a×c)/(b×d).

items.title: Converting Mixed Fractions
items.explanation: When calculating distances involving mixed fractions, convert them into improper fractions first. For example, if the tortoise walks 1 1/4 km in 1 hour, this is equivalent to 5/4 km. To find the distance in 1 1/2 hours, multiply 5/4 by 3 (the numerator of the multiplier) to get 15/4, which converts back to a mixed fraction.
